title: Sisyphus — The tale itself
summary: Sisyphus was condemned to roll a boulder uphill forever, watching it roll back down. This study tells the myth straight and complete.
body:
Sisyphus was condemned to roll a boulder uphill forever, watching it roll back down. Camus made him the emblem of the absurd.

Every myth deserves to be heard as story first. Sisyphus unfolds with its own logic — characters acting from motives the myth takes for granted, events following one another with dreamlike necessity. To know Sisyphus is to be able to tell it. Viewed through a narrative lens, Sisyphus is examined as story — its plot, its pacing, and the moments that make it unforgettable.

The story is the data. All interpretation comes after, and must answer to the tale as told. A fourth sub-question examines the moral the myth was meant to teach its first hearers. Related entries in this archive: Set and Maat.
key_points: The full narrative of Sisyphus preserved.
